questions.question: In pipelined processor microarchitecture, what fundamentally characterizes a structural hazard?
options: A dependent instruction attempts to read a register before an earlier instruction in the pipeline has written its result back to the register file.
The processor encounters a conditional branch or jump instruction whose target address or outcome is not yet resolved.
Two or more concurrent instructions in different pipeline stages require access to the exact same physical hardware resource in the same clock cycle.
Successive instructions attempt to write to the same architectural destination register in an order that violates program semantics.
An instruction raises a hardware exception during execution, requiring subsequent instructions in the pipeline to be flushed.

questions.question: In deep-submicron CMOS physical design and fabrication, what is the 'antenna effect' (plasma-induced damage), and how is it standardly mitigated during routing?
options: Electromagnetic radiation emitted by high-frequency clock routes induces capacitive crosstalk; it is resolved by routing continuous VDD or VSS shielding traces alongside victim nets.

Charge accumulation on long unconnected metal routes during plasma etching can rupture thin gate dielectric; it is resolved by routing metal jumpers to higher layers or inserting reverse-biased protection diodes.
Inductive reflections occurring on long inter-block wires cause signal ringing and overshoot; it is resolved by inserting series source termination resistors at the driver output.
Substrate noise generated by fast-switching digital logic couples into sensitive analog circuitry; it is resolved by placing deep N-well guard rings around sensitive regions.
Voltage drop along power delivery grids fluctuates due to excessive trace resistance; it is resolved by inserting localized decoupling capacitors beneath dense routing channels.

questions.question: In Static Timing Analysis (STA) of synchronous digital circuits, under what operational condition is a designer justified in defining a Multi-Cycle Path (MCP) constraint, and what is its effect on timing checks?
options: When signals transfer between completely asynchronous clock domains; it disables both setup and hold timing checks across the boundary.
When a combinational data path is logically impossible to activate under any valid state; it excludes the path entirely from timing analysis reports.
When clock tree synthesis (CTS) yields excessive insertion delay on the launch flop; it forces the timing tool to balance the clock network over multiple cycles.

When control logic ensures that the destination register samples the transmitted data only after N > 1 clock cycles; it relaxes the setup timing requirement to N clock cycles while appropriately shifting the hold check.
When dynamic IR drop causes transient propagation delays along critical paths; it dynamically stretches the operational clock period for those specific paths during static verification.

questions.question: In high-performance microprocessor microarchitecture, how does Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) fundamentally differ from fine-grained temporal multithreading (interleaved multithreading)?
options: SMT issues instructions from multiple active threads concurrently to different execution units within the exact same clock cycle, whereas fine-grained multithreading interleaves instructions from different threads on alternate clock cycles.
SMT requires dedicated, non-shared execution units and ALUs for each architectural thread, whereas fine-grained multithreading uses time-multiplexed sharing of a single execution pipeline.
SMT switches execution to another thread only when the running thread stalls on a long-latency event such as an LLC miss, whereas fine-grained multithreading switches threads every single cycle.

SMT relies exclusively on static compiler analysis to pack instructions from independent threads into wide instruction packets, whereas fine-grained multithreading handles thread dispatch dynamically.
SMT replicates the shared L2 and L3 caches for each hardware thread context, whereas fine-grained multithreading shares a single unified cache hierarchy across all threads.

questions.question: In bulk CMOS integrated circuit technology, what physical phenomenon causes the parasitic 'latchup' condition, and what layout methodology is primarily used to prevent it?
options: Trap-assisted tunneling through the ultra-thin gate dielectric; prevented by replacing standard SiO2 gate oxides with high-k metal gate dielectric stacks.
Hot-carrier degradation occurring at the drain pinch-off region; prevented by incorporating lightly doped drain (LDD) implant extensions.
Thermal runaway triggered by excessive localized power density; prevented by distributing dummy metal fills and thermal conduction vias throughout the floorplan.
Dielectric breakdown induced by electrostatic discharge (ESD) events at I/O pads; prevented by attaching series current-limiting ballasting resistors to pad drivers.

Regenerative forward-biasing of a parasitic p-n-p-n thyristor structure formed by cross-coupled bipolar transistors; prevented by placing frequent well and substrate taps to keep substrate resistance low.
